I've spent the last six years owning products end-to-end, from early concept through scaled delivery, and building alignment across engineers, designers, and stakeholders without relying on direct authority. That's the core of what this Order Quality role asks for, and it's the kind of work I do well.

At Starling Bank, I owned the Faster Payments integration and cut settlement failures by 34%, leading a team of 6 engineers and 2 designers through the full arc from problem definition to shipped, measurable improvement. At Revolut, I launched card controls that reached 2.1 million customers and redesigned the claims flow to reduce chargeback disputes by 18%. Both cases required the same thing this role demands: defining success metrics, prioritizing ruthlessly, and communicating tradeoffs clearly enough that cross-functional teams could move fast together.

My background is in payments rather than grocery or physical retail, but the underlying discipline transfers directly: understanding a two-sided experience, protecting trust on both sides of a transaction, and using data to decide what matters most when priorities compete.

I'd welcome a short call to talk through how this experience maps to Order Quality's roadmap and where I could add the most value early on.

I'd bring that same approach to aligning Instacart's cross-functional Order Quality team around a shared roadmap.

I'd welcome a conversation about where this role is headed and how my payments background might translate to the fulfillment space. Happy to find a time that works.

I'd welcome a short call to talk through where my background fits and where it doesn't, and to hear more about what the team needs right now.
